correctness.rationale: For d=2^(2m)+1 the 2m distinct coordinates a_j=2^(j+1)/d lie below 1/2 except the last, 1-1/d. The tent map doubles up to the last and sends it back to a_0. This includes m=1. Increasing PL homeomorphisms h and k map the even and odd subsequences to the respective sorted prescribed points, with endpoints fixed. Thus k T h^(-1) and h T k^(-1) are onto, strictly unimodal PL, and have the specified endpoints and peaks. The return maps are conjugate to T^2, whose powers have full branches at arbitrarily fine dyadic scales, proving exactness on the whole interval. For a countable basis, the union of iterated preimages of each basis interval under the second return map's m-th power is open and dense, by exactness, even if any prescribed finite initial segment is removed. Baire therefore gives a coordinate y with every orbit tail dense under that power. On each even residue phase mod m the first coordinate is fixed at p_i and the second coordinate has dense tails by the corresponding surjective iterate; hence the even omega set is exactly P×I. Continuity and compactness give the odd omega set as the image of the even one, I×Q. There is no requirement that P and Q be disjoint, and the construction does not impose one.
residual_risks: The finite exact-rational diagnostic checks interpolation and identities only. Universal exactness and infinite orbit density are proved analytically.
The theorem concerns full-span lattices of interior prescribed points; no proper-subspan or logistic-family claim was established.

value.rationale: This settles a natural full-span case of the explicit unimodality question, uniformly for arbitrary locations and cardinality, with the least possible number of turning points for onto reactions having both endpoints zero. The alternating orbit and independent PL changes of coordinates give a reusable realization technique without the many branches of the unrestricted construction. It does not settle proper-support or logistic-family realization.
residual_risks: Value is in the proved full-span restriction, not in the known unconstrained realization or in a resolution of the full open problem.
